title: Critical theta-half Gibbs cancellation and local second-moment bound
question: At the critical fractional exponent theta=1/2, does the Gibbs relation exactly cancel the doubled-bond transition energy and reduce the Kubo-Mori shell to a local Gibbs second-moment bound?
method: Use the actual-Q3 V=2 edge at d=3,4,5,6 and V=4 square at d=2 with all translated measured sites and selected bonds, both split orientations, signs, history adjoints, beta values and all prefix positions.
Diagonalize each doubled bond generator and construct finite Gibbs logarithmic-mean weights, using the diagonal limit at equal energies.
Check the identity L_ij*|lambda_i-lambda_j|=|p_i-p_j|/beta and bound the resulting square-function by (4/beta) sum_i p_i sum_j |X_ij|^2 for every centered witness.
Rebuild the complete finite table in a non-importing independent lane and compile Lean R371 for the scalar cancellation, positive pair inequality, finite pair bound and scope only.
finding: Primary and independent lanes each pass 14235/14235 assertions over 2816 all-prefix contexts; the integrated verifier passes 129/129 and Lean R371 passes. The largest primary-independent numeric difference is 2.771e-13, the maximum Gibbs identity error is 2.689e-17, and the local second-moment bound has no positive violation. The largest sampled local Gibbs second moment is 42.156906839727924 at edge d=6, after 2.751158478344597, 3.43464599148746 and 4.704458970507892 at d=3,4,5.
decision_reason: The critical theta-half identity removes the explicit transition-energy factor exactly and identifies the true analytic input for the direct D,delta-D route: a uniform local Gibbs second-moment estimate on a Hamiltonian-derived common core. The finite second moment grows on the sampled edge cutoff sequence, so this input is not silently promoted to a uniform theorem.

adversarial_review.check: Equal eigenvalues use the p_i limiting convention and no zero logarithmic gap is divided in either executable lane.
Absolute transition energy and probability difference are used, so reversing the eigenvalue order leaves the identity unchanged.
The row-sum identity is evaluated in the finite bond Gibbs eigenbasis; no commutation of the full interacting Gibbs state through X is assumed.
The ratio is only a diagnostic and the loose one-sided pair bound is not treated as saturation.
The local second moment rises to 42.1569 at d=6; finite rows are not promoted to a cutoff-independent estimate.
The independent lane reconstructs oscillator, graph, Gibbs weights, spectra, witnesses and prefixes without importing primary R-371.
Lean R371 formalizes scalar cancellation and positive pair inequalities only; numerical spectra, trace limits and common cores remain outside the kernel.
Uniform second moment, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Prove a source-, volume- and cutoff-uniform local Gibbs second-moment estimate on a Hamiltonian-derived common core, then combine R-371 with the R-370 frequency split for the direct D,delta-D corridor.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite critical-theta Gibbs-cancellation checkpoint only. The doubled local bond Gibbs state is not a global KMS state; uniform second moment, cutoff/volume/source/shape control, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
no_overclaim: R-371 closes the finite algebraic reduction but does not close its uniform moment premise or any QFT/Clay gate.
